ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Sick Visit — Ernest Shackleton

code.originalText: Same-day sick visit for low back pain

text.paragraph: Low back pain for two days after lifting crates at the dock. [S]

Mr. Shackleton asked for a same-day visit for low back pain that began two days ago while he was lifting crates of stores onto the ship, after his crew had left for the day. The pain is a deep ache across the lower back, worse on the left, worse with bending and getting out of a chair, and eased by lying flat and walking slowly. It does not go down his legs. He has no numbness, weakness, numbness in the saddle area, or change in bladder or bowel control, no fever, and no fall. He has had no chest pain, breathlessness, or palpitations, including while lifting, and he has not needed nitroglycerin. He has not taken ibuprofen, because he was told not to with his blood thinners, and acetaminophen has helped a little. He has no muscle aches elsewhere. He is worried he will not be fit to sail in three weeks. [S]

list.item:
Acute low back strain (S39.012A). Mechanical low back pain after lifting, with no sciatica, neurological deficit, or red flags, so no imaging is needed. NSAIDs are avoided: with aspirin and clopidogrel they raise the risk of bleeding, and they add cardiovascular risk. The pain is one-sided and mechanical, with no diffuse aching or weakness, so statin muscle toxicity is unlikely and a CK test is not needed. Most strains settle within two to four weeks. [S]
Heat, and keep moving; avoid bed rest.
Acetaminophen 1 g up to three times a day, no more than 3 g a day.
No NSAIDs, including over-the-counter ibuprofen and naproxen.
Pause the resistance part of cardiac rehabilitation for a week and keep the walking.
No lifting of crates; delegate loading.
Return at once for leg weakness, numbness in the saddle area, loss of bladder or bowel control, or fever.

Chronic coronary disease with a stent (I25.118). No angina while lifting. Blood pressure a little higher today with pain. [S]
Pre-departure review in two weeks as planned.
